about.intro_content: Prof. An-Kui Yang is a Professor in the Department of Head and Neck Surgery at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center (SYSUCC), Guangzhou, with extensive experience treating thyroid, laryngeal, tongue, salivary gland and paranasal sinus cancers.
about.detailed_content: Prof. Yang has published extensively on head and neck cancer surgical outcomes, including laryngeal reconstruction techniques after extensive partial laryngectomy, anaplastic thyroid carcinoma treatment and prognosis, and free flap transfer for defect repair after salvage surgery. His research has examined prognostic biomarkers such as COX-2 and P300 expression in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma, and molecular markers for papillary thyroid carcinoma.

faq.section_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Prof. An-Kui Yang

items.question: Does Prof. An-Kui Yang accept international patients?
items.answer: CancerFax can coordinate medical report review and consultation support for international patients seeking an opinion related to head and neck cancer at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, subject to hospital availability and case acceptance.

items.question: What is Prof. Yang's area of specialisation?
items.answer: Prof. Yang specialises in the surgical treatment of thyroid cancer, laryngeal cancer, tongue cancer, salivary gland cancer and paranasal sinus cancer.

items.question: How can I request a consultation or second opinion?
items.answer: Submit your medical reports through CancerFax. The CancerFax team reviews the documents, prepares the case for submission, and coordinates next steps with SYSUCC's International Medical Center, subject to availability.

items.question: Does Prof. Yang treat anaplastic thyroid carcinoma?
items.answer: Yes. Prof. Yang has published outcomes research on the treatment and prognosis of anaplastic thyroid carcinoma, one of the most aggressive forms of thyroid cancer.

items.question: Does Prof. Yang perform reconstructive surgery after laryngeal cancer surgery?
items.answer: Yes. Prof. Yang has published techniques for laryngeal reconstruction, including combined hyoid bone flap methods, to preserve function after extensive partial laryngectomy.
